result.topic_en: Euler derives, for an elastic curve, the relations V = C sin φ and T = C cos φ, integrates to obtain ds in terms of φ, finds the radius of osculation, and begins converting to orthogonal coordinates.
result.transcription:
402 DE STATV AEQVILIBRII ET MOTV
det a certa quadam directione fixa, quae quum penitus
arbitrio nostro relinquatur ea ita capiatur vt fiat $D=0$,
sicque iam adepti sumus has duas formulas satis simpli-
ces $V=C\sin.\phi$ et $T=C\cos.\phi$, his autem litteris bi-
nae illae vires exprimuntur, quibus status cuiusque ele-
menti $Mm$ definitur, quae ergo vbique ita sunt compara-
tae vt sit $TT+VV=CC$ siue vis illis aequiualens
constans.
XXX. His inuentis iam supra vidimus ex tertia ae-
quatione fieri $V=\frac{A\,dd\phi}{ds^2}=C\sin.\phi$, sumto $ds$ constante, quae
per $2d\phi$ multiplicata et integrata praebet: $\frac{A\,d\phi^2}{ds^2}=B-2C.\cos.\phi$,
hincque $\frac{d\phi}{ds}=\sqrt{\left(\frac{B-2C\cos.\phi}{A}\right)}$, siue $ds=\frac{d\phi\sqrt{A}}{\sqrt{(B-2C.\cos.\phi)}}$, quae
aequatio duas tantum variabiles continet $\phi$ et $s$, vbi $s$
denotat arcum curuae AM a puncto quodam fixo compu-
tatum; angulus $\phi$ vero exprimit amplitudinem huius ar-
cus. Deinde possumus etiam radium osculi curuae defini-
re, qui si ponatur $=r$, ob $d\phi=\frac{ds}{r}$, aequatio inuenta
ostendit fore $r=\frac{\sqrt{A}}{\sqrt{(B-2C\cos\phi)}}$, vnde patet sumto $\phi=0$,
fieri radium osculi $r=\sqrt{\frac{A}{B-2C}}$.
XXXI. Hinc etiam facile possumus progredi ad coor-
dinatas orthogonales, si enim axem AX ita ducamus vt
fiat angulus $AMX=\phi$, tum quia $dx=ds\sin.\phi$, et
$dy=ds\cos.\phi$ sequentem habebimus aequationem:
$dx=\frac{d\phi\sin.\phi.\sqrt{A}}{\sqrt{(B-2C.\cos.\phi)}}$,
quae

items.quote: sicque iam adepti sumus has duas formulas satis simplices $V=C\sin.\phi$ et $T=C\cos.\phi$
items.english: And thus we have now obtained these two fairly simple formulas V = C sin φ and T = C cos φ.

items.quote: quae ergo vbique ita sunt comparatae vt sit $TT+VV=CC$ siue vis illis aequiualens constans.
items.english: These forces are therefore everywhere such that TT + VV = CC, i.e. the force equivalent to them is constant.

items.quote: Deinde possumus etiam radium osculi curuae definire
items.english: Next we can also determine the radius of osculation of the curve.

items.quote: Hinc etiam facile possumus progredi ad coordinatas orthogonales
items.english: From here we can also easily proceed to orthogonal coordinates.
